claims.text:
max-entropy-irl

**Identity / target / source:** `ai:max-entropy-irl` → `ai-max-entropy-irl` → `src/demos/ai/ai-max-entropy-irl`; source `company/domains/proposals/2026-10-18-ai-map-expansion.json#concepts/118`; brief `company/domains/briefs/2026-10-19-ai-next30e.md#14-max-entropy-irl`. **Packet:** R2. **Level / prerequisites:** stretch; `ai:reward-ambiguity`, `ai:boltzmann-rational-demos`.

**Nearest / distinct payoff:** reward-ambiguity establishes compatible rewards; this computes entropy-maximizing trajectory distributions under an explicit feature expectation.

**Computed primary model:** Four feasible trajectories with scalar feature counts[0,1,1,2]. Constraint expected feature=1. Uniform[.25,.25,.25,.25] satisfies it and entropyln4; alternative[.5,0,0,.5] also satisfies it but entropyln2. In reward class r_i=theta*f_i+c, Boltzmann distributionp_i=exp(theta*f_i)/Z gives theta0 for mean1. Shiftc by any constant leaves normalized probabilities unchanged.

**Countercase / boundary:** Change expectation to1.5: theta=ln3 gives probabilities[1,3,3,9]/16 and feature mean1.5. Maximum entropy is relative to the specified feasible trajectories/base measure; it does not uniquely identify an underlying human reward. Do not assert uniformity for a changed constraint or inaccessible path set.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict which mean1 distribution is less committed beyond the constraint; recall adding7 to all rewards changes no normalized trajectory probabilities.

**Intervention / retained witness:** Select same-mean alternatives computes entropy and expectation separately; Change constraint derives normalized Boltzmann masses and new mean. Retain equal-expectation/different-entropy witness and constant-shift invariance. All path features/reachability are declared inputs.

**Source obligation:** [Ziebart et al. original PDF](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~bziebart/publications/maximum-entropy-inverse-reinforcement-learning.pdf), opened2026-10-19, maximum entropy under feature matching and trajectory distribution. This finite4-path calculation supplies no real demonstrator assumptions or causal-entropy extension.
